bound_direction.cost: NAMED, NOT GLOSSED. Both Y legs inherit condition (b)'s own lack of a confidence bound, so a Y coverage decision at small n is exactly as noisy as (b) itself. That noise belongs to the FROZEN criterion. Correcting it would mean moving a pre-registered threshold after seeing the data it governs, which is the researcher degree of freedom pre-registration exists to remove. It is RECORDED here and deliberately NOT fixed.
bound_direction.reported_lower_bounds_note: wilson_lower_bound exists in scripts/phase20_gate_coverage.py for REPORTING only, in scripts/erasure_gate.py:161-168's rule_of_three register: published ALONGSIDE the deciding statistic and never instead of it. coverage_verdict reads it nowhere. The fixture Y points are fabricated RATES carrying no count, so each bound is priced at the nearest whole count at n = 104 and that count is published beside it; the bound is a report about the criterion's precision, not an input to any decision.
bound_direction.resolution: CRITERION-MATCHING PER AXIS (D-37), not 'always use the tighter bound'. The extraction axis reads wilson_upper_bound because condition (a) at mitigation_gate.py:755-756 is DECIDED on it. Both recall legs read the RAW rate because condition (b) at mitigation_gate.py:767-768 is DECIDED on it. A Wilson LOWER bound on a floor would decide coverage on a statistic the criterion does not read — CR-01's own defect class with the sign flipped — and it would invert the conservatism of a floor criterion.

zero_successes_short_circuit.reason: wilson_lower_bound opens with `if successes == 0: return 0.0`, and it is ANALYTICALLY EXACT rather than a fudge: at p = 0 the algebra gives centre == spread identically (both z^2/2n), so Wilson's lower bound at zero successes IS exactly 0. The unrounded mirror leaves a POSITIVE residue, measured at n = 104 above, so max(0.0, ...) passes it through untouched. The divergence from an exact mirror is declared here and in the function's own docstring so a later reader 'restoring the symmetry' is warned off (T-20-53).

y_leg_differential.mechanism: nan >= 0.24499999999999997 is False, so the NaN was COUNTED as a FAILING point beside 0.28's clearing one and MANUFACTURED the bracket that the strictly LESS truncated honest sweep lacks. It did not pass through; it produced the coverage. A NaN recall is what 0/0 yields from an empty held-out question set, so this is a reachable input rather than a contrived one. The per-element [0.0, 1.0] range check subsumes NaN with no special-case branch a later reader can delete.
